topics.title: LTS Timeline
topics.description: Interviewers love the "what's new in Java" question, especially since Java 21 (Sep 2023 LTS) and Java 25 (Sep 2025 LTS). Know which release owns which headline feature.

rows: Sealed classes, records (finalized 16), pattern matching for instanceof
Virtual threads, record patterns, pattern matching for switch, sequenced collections
Scoped values, flexible constructor bodies, compact source files, module import declarations

topics.title: Virtual Threads
topics.description: Java 21's headline feature. Lightweight threads managed by the JVM, not the OS. Millions can run on a few carrier (platform) threads.
topics.how_they_work: When a virtual thread blocks on I/O, its stack is unmounted from the carrier thread and parked in the heap; the carrier picks up another virtual thread. Blocking becomes cheap, so you can write simple blocking code with async-level scalability.

talking_points.title: I/O-bound only
talking_points.description: Made for I/O-bound workloads such as HTTP calls and DB queries. CPU-bound work gains nothing.

talking_points.title: Do not pool them
talking_points.description: Create one virtual thread per task. Pooling defeats the purpose.

talking_points.title: Pinning
talking_points.description: A virtual thread cannot unmount inside synchronized blocks that block, or inside native calls, so it pins the carrier. Fix: use ReentrantLock instead of synchronized around blocking calls. Java 24 largely removed the synchronized pinning limitation, but mention the concept.

talking_points.title: ThreadLocal cost
talking_points.description: ThreadLocal still works but is costly at millions of threads. Scoped Values are the successor.

talking_points.title: Spring Boot 3.2+
talking_points.description: Setting spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true puts Tomcat request handling on virtual threads.

pooling_virtual_threads.bad:
// Pooling virtual threads defeats the purpose
var executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(200, Thread.ofVirtual().factory());
pooling_virtual_threads.good:
// One virtual thread per task — creation is cheap
var executor = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor();

topics.title: Records
topics.description: Immutable data carriers introduced in the Java 17 era and still asked about constantly. Final fields, accessors, equals, hashCode and toString are generated.
key_points: Immutable data carriers: final fields plus generated accessors, equals, hashCode and toString.
Great for DTOs and query projections.
JPA entities cannot be records: JPA needs a no-arg constructor and mutable state.
A compact constructor is the place to put validation.

hand_written_class_vs_record.good: public record Money(BigDecimal amount, Currency currency) { }

topics.title: Sealed Types
topics.description: Closed hierarchies: the compiler knows every subtype, which enables exhaustive switch without a default branch.
topics.code:
public sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Square, Rectangle {}
public record Circle(double radius) implements Shape {}
key_points: permits lists the only allowed subtypes.
The compiler enforces exhaustiveness over an enum or a sealed hierarchy, so default becomes unnecessary.
Adding a new subtype turns every switch into a compile error - a feature, not a bug.
Records plus sealed types plus pattern matching is what the industry calls data-oriented programming.

topics.title: Pattern Matching
topics.description: From instanceof patterns in Java 16 to switch patterns with record deconstruction and guards in Java 21.

code.title: switch with patterns, records and guards (Java 21)

topics.data_oriented_programming: Records plus sealed types plus pattern-matched switch is data-oriented programming - the umbrella term worth dropping in interviews. It makes domain modelling exhaustive and terse.

topics.title: Java 21 Extras
topics.description: The smaller Java 21 items that still come up, plus the one feature you should not claim shipped.
sequenced_collections: The SequencedCollection interface adds getFirst(), getLast() and reversed().
Implemented by List, Deque and LinkedHashSet.
Replaces the old assortment of first/last idioms that differed per collection.
topics.string_templates: Previewed in 21 and withdrawn in 23 for redesign. Do not cite it as a shipped feature.

topics.title: Structured Concurrency
topics.description: StructuredTaskScope treats a group of subtasks as one unit: if one fails the siblings are cancelled, and results are joined in one place. Still preview or incubating through 25 - call it a preview.

topics.title: Scoped Values
topics.description: Final in Java 25. Immutable per-thread context that stays cheap with virtual threads - the ThreadLocal successor.
key_points: Immutable: the value is bound for the duration of a call, not mutated in place.
No cleanup or leak risk, unlike ThreadLocal.
Cheap at the scale virtual threads make possible.

topics.title: Java 22-25 Highlights
topics.description: The features shipped between the two LTS releases, and which version made each one final.

rows: Custom intermediate stream ops via Stream.gather(...) - windowing, folding
Standard bytecode parsing and generation (replaces ASM for the JDK)
Immutable per-thread context, cheap with virtual threads - the ThreadLocal successor
Statements allowed before super(...) - validate before calling super
Compact source files and instance main
void main() { ... } without class boilerplate - beginner-friendly entry points
import module java.base; - import a whole module's exports
ZGC collects the young generation separately

topics.title: Answer Framework
topics.description: How to answer "what's new in Java that excites you?" in about 60 seconds.

structure.title: 1. Virtual threads
structure.description: Changed how we write scalable I/O code, and Spring Boot enables them with a single property.

structure.title: 2. Data-oriented programming
structure.description: Records plus sealed types plus pattern-matched switch make domain modelling exhaustive and terse.

structure.title: 3. Java 25 LTS
structure.description: Scoped values as the ThreadLocal successor and flexible constructors. Mention your team's upgrade path, for example "we're on 17, evaluating 21 to 25".

topics.title: Interview Questions
topics.description: The four questions this material is most often tested with.

questions.question: Virtual threads vs platform threads?
questions.description: Platform threads are 1:1 with OS threads, have roughly 1MB stacks and top out in the thousands. Virtual threads are JVM-scheduled over carrier threads, have heap-allocated stacks, can number in the millions, and make blocking cheap. Same Thread API.

questions.question: Do virtual threads replace reactive programming?
questions.description: Largely, for I/O concurrency: blocking style with virtual threads reaches similar throughput with far simpler code and stack traces. Reactive still wins for streaming and backpressure semantics. Balanced answers score points.

questions.question: Why can't a JPA entity be a record?
questions.description: Records are immutable and have no no-arg constructor; JPA requires a no-arg constructor and field mutation via proxies. Records are ideal for projections and DTOs instead.

questions.question: When is default unnecessary in a switch?
questions.description: When the selector is an enum or a sealed hierarchy and all cases are covered. The compiler enforces exhaustiveness, and adding a new subtype becomes a compile error at every switch - a feature, not a bug.
